title: Page reloads or redirects itself after a delay (AAA)
user_impact: Users are interrupted: the page changes without a request, and screen reader users lose their reading position.
technical_impact: A <meta http-equiv="refresh"> with a delay above 0 reloads or redirects the page after that delay, also above 20 hours.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.4 Interruptions and SC 3.2.5 Change on Request (AAA); technique H76/F40/F41; HTML 'shared declarative refresh steps'; ACT bisz58
checks.applicability: The first meta element with http-equiv=refresh (any case) whose content starts with digits, also when inserted by script.
checks.expectation:
Fails at the meta element when it reloads or redirects after any delay above
0, also 20 hours or more: the 20-hour exception of 2.2.1 does not apply at
AAA, and a change the user did not request interrupts them. Content without
leading digits is ignored by browsers and passes. A delay of 0 is an
immediate redirect, not an interruption; it is not exercised in the corpus
because it would navigate the fixture away. Only the first valid refresh
counts, as in the browser.
